title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
why_read: A new model-agnostic interpretability method that avoids needing model weights or labeled concept datasets is a solid, practically useful contribution to explainable AI.
analysis: Hide and Seek (HnS) is a technique for explaining what visual concepts drive a black-box vision model's output, without needing access to the model's internal weights or large hand-labeled datasets of concepts. It works by finding images containing a target concept, masking that concept region, and measuring how much the model's output changes, giving a causal attribution signal. This extends concept-based explanation beyond classification to tasks like image captioning and satellite segmentation, which prior methods couldn't handle. The validation against ground-truth attributions on CelebA and COCO-Stuff gives some confidence the method is measuring something real rather than just plausible-looking explanations.
